item.title: Niger miners’ deaths: Senate demands sanctions, compensation
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has urged the Federal Government to expedite the implementation of recommendations made by the independent investigative committee into the deaths of 37 artisanal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Niger State. The lawmakers specifically called for accountability, appropriate sanctions against officers found culpable and institutional reforms within the NSCDC, warning that further delay in implementing the recommendations could undermine public confidence in the government’s commitment to justice. The Senate also stressed the need for prompt payment of financial compensation recommended for the families of the deceased. The resolutions followed a motion on Wednesday sponsored by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Finance, Senator Sani Musa (APC, Niger East), and co-sponsored by 18 other senators from the North-Central geopolitical zone and Senator Nasir Sani Zango Daura (APC, Katsina North). The Senate commended President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Government for establishing an independent investigative committee to probe the incident and acknowledged that the 10-member panel, chaired by Jonathan Kure, had submitted its report. The committee reportedly identified serious lapses and recommended sanctions, institutional reforms and financial compensation for the victims’ families and other affected persons. The lawmakers recalled that the 37 miners died on September 17, 2026, while in NSCDC custody in Minna, Niger State, after reportedly being arrested during operations against suspected illegal mining activities. They expressed concern that the circumstances surrounding the deaths raised serious questions about the protection of fundamental human rights and the responsibility of security agencies to safeguard persons in their custody. The Senate warned that any further delay in implementing the committee’s recommendations, particularly the payment of compensation, would prolong the suffering of the bereaved families. It also called for comprehensive reforms in the management of detention facilities and the operational procedures of security agencies to prevent a recurrence. Seconding the motion, Senator Ned Nwoko (APC, Delta North) described the incident as a national tragedy, insisting that the circumstances of the deaths should be examined objectively, irrespective of the alleged activities of the deceased. He said: “It is a national tragedy when so many young lives are lost under circumstances such as the ones we are discussing.” Nwoko, who drew parallels with incidents involving young people allegedly engaged in illegal activities in oil-producing communities in the South-South, said the country must apply consistent standards in addressing such cases. He added: “The fact that some of these young men may have been involved in illegal activities should not mean that their lives are not valued. “Life is life, regardless of the circumstances. item.title: 2027: APM governorship candidate mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Laja Adeoye, has expressed sadness over the death of Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, popularly known as Femi Ajasa, Online Editor of Vanguard Media Limited. Ajasa died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness. He was aged 44. Adeoye, who disclosed this in a condolence statement on Wednesday, described the late journalist as a professional who demonstrated passion, integrity and commitment to truth in the discharge of his duties. He said Ajasa approached journalism with dedication and professionalism, adding that his contributions to Vanguard and the wider media industry would not be forgotten. The APM governorship candidate, who described himself as an advocate of press freedom, said a free and responsible press remained indispensable to democracy. He noted that journalists like Ajasa embodied the values that made press freedom meaningful, pledging his continued support for media practitioners and the protection of press freedom. Adeoye said the deceased would be greatly missed by his colleagues at Vanguard, members of the Nigerian media community and all those who knew and worked with him. He extended his condolences to Ajasa’s family, friends and the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, praying God to grant them the strength to bear the loss and for the repose of the deceased’s soul. item.title: Tinubu approves world’s first PR university, says Nigeria bigger than 419
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of what he described as the world’s first University of Public Relations and Leadership, as part of efforts to develop a new generation of communication professionals through specialised education, research and professional training. Tinubu announced the approval in a speech delivered by Vice President Kashim Shettima at the 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja. The President said a major outcome of Nigeria’s hosting of the global forum was the determination to establish a lasting institutional legacy for the public relations profession. He said: “In this regard, I am pleased to formally approve and support the establishment of the University of Public Relations and Leadership, a first-of-its-kind initiative designed to advance specialised education, research, professional development and leadership training in public relations, strategic communications and related disciplines.” He described the proposed institution as a major investment in human capital and the future of communication, adding that it would provide opportunities to develop communication leaders capable of responding to the demands of a rapidly changing global environment. Tinubu commended the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations, the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation, and the Nasarawa State Government for their collaboration and commitment to the initiative. He urged stakeholders to work together to ensure that the institution developed into a centre of excellence. The President also expressed Nigeria’s appreciation to the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and the international public relations community for entrusting the country with the hosting of the global gathering. He described the decision as recognition of Nigeria’s growing contribution to the global communication profession and its capacity to promote responsible communication. Tinubu said hosting the forum provided an opportunity to showcase Nigeria’s people, cultural diversity, economic potential and commitment to constructive international engagement. Addressing the changing communication landscape, the President said digital technologies and artificial intelligence were transforming how information was created, distributed and consumed. He, however, warned that the developments had also created challenges, including misinformation, disinformation, hate speech and declining public trust. “In this environment, public relations and communication professionals have responsibilities that go beyond managing images and reputations,” he said. According to him, communication professionals must promote truth, accountability, transparency, mutual understanding and constructive engagement between governments, institutions and citizens. item.title: Chimamanda’s son’s death: Coroner resumes inquest
item.description: The coroner’s inquest into the death of Nkanu Adichie-Esege, son of Nigerian author Chimamanda Adichie and her husband, Ivara Esege, resumed on Wednesday at the Igbosere Magistrate’s Court in Lagos following a Lagos High Court ruling affirming the coroner’s jurisdiction. The coroner, Magistrate Atinuke Adetunji, resumed proceedings after the High Court dismissed an application by Euracare Hospital seeking to stop the inquest. At Wednesday’s sitting, Taiwo Osipitan, counsel to Euracare Hospital, said it was the first time all parties were appearing before the coroner following the conclusion of proceedings at the High Court. Osipitan said the High Court had ruled that the matter had not reached the stage at which judicial review was necessary and directed that the case be returned to the coroner’s court for continuation of the inquest. He subsequently tendered a copy of the High Court judgment before Adetunji. However, Chukwudi Enebeli, counsel to the deceased’s family, told the court that Euracare’s application was struck out because the coroner’s court had jurisdiction to proceed with the inquest. Enebeli sought an adjournment, explaining that Euracare had only served the parties in open court with the witness statement on oath of Tosin Majekodunmi, a medical doctor. He said the family needed time to examine the statement and determine whether a response would be necessary. Abiodun Loyonu, counsel to Atlantis Paediatric Hospital, also asked the court for an opportunity to respond to Euracare’s witness statement. In her response, the magistrate reminded the parties that the inquest was inquisitorial in nature, adding that guidelines for conducting the proceedings had been discussed at a preliminary meeting held at the commencement of the inquiry. She urged all parties to bear the distinctive nature of the proceedings in mind as the inquest progressed. The coroner also asked whether the parties had filed witness statements on oath in preparation for the hearing. Osipitan, however, sought clarification on whether Lagos State Government officials would be required to file witness statements on oath or could appear in court to give oral evidence if subpoenaed. Adetunji said filing witness statements on oath was not mandatory for such witnesses, adding that government officials summoned through subpoenas could appear before the court and give oral evidence. The parties subsequently agreed that the deceased’s family would lead evidence, followed by Atlantis Paediatric Hospital and Euracare Hospital. The coroner adjourned the inquest to January 19, 20 and 28, 2027. Nkanu, one of Adichie’s twins, died on January 7, 2026, following complications during a series of preparatory medical procedures at Euracare Hospital after being referred from Atlantis Paediatric Hospital. item.title: ADC campaign accuses INEC of bias, demands postponement of mock election test
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, has accused the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, of giving political parties inadequate notice for its November 28 mock accreditation and results collation exercise, demanding its postponement. The Council said the short notice would make it difficult for parties to mobilise, train and deploy agents for the nationwide exercise, warning that the process could undermine confidence in a test designed to assess electoral technology ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC also faulted INEC’s reported decision not to upload results from Ward, Local Government and State collation levels to its Result Viewing Portal, IReV, during the 2027 elections. The Council said INEC’s November 16 notification, coming barely two days before the November 18 deadline for submitting agents’ names, was unfair, particularly as the exercise would cover all 774 Local Government Areas and two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 Registration Areas. “How does INEC expect political parties to adequately prepare, mobilise, train and submit their agents for an exercise of this magnitude within such a short time? This is not preparation; it is an ambush,” the Council queried. “INEC cannot test electoral credibility through an incredible process.” It demanded an immediate postponement to give political parties sufficient time to nominate agents and participate meaningfully. On electronic transmission of results, the ADC-PCC rejected comments reportedly made by INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, that the Commission had neither developed nor tested the system for uploading results from the various collation levels. “Nigerians fought for and demanded real-time electronic transmission of election results precisely to eliminate the manipulation that often occurs between the Polling Unit and subsequent collation levels. “Any attempt to weaken, delay or abandon electronic transmission and public visibility of results at the various levels of collation is an invitation to electoral manipulation,” the Council warned. It recalled that former INEC Chairman, Professor Mahmood Yakubu, had promised to extend result uploads to Ward, Local Government and State levels, adding that his successor, Professor Joash Amupitan, SAN, had also pledged to strengthen electoral transparency. Questioning the Commission’s apparent change of position, the ADC-PCC asked: “What has changed? Why the sudden retreat from commitments previously made to Nigerians?” It further questioned why Forms EC8B (Ward), EC8C (Local Government) and EC8D (State) could not be uploaded to IReV when the Commission already had the technology to upload polling-unit results on Form EC8A. item.title: Tinubu transmits bill to Reps to decriminalise attempted suicide
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has transmitted the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026, to the House of Representatives for consideration, seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide and provide support for persons who attempt to take their lives. The President’s request was contained in a letter dated November 10, 2026, addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, and read on the floor of the House during plenary on Wednesday. In the letter, Tinubu said the proposed legislation seeks to amend the National Mental Health Act, No. 46, 2021, to remove the criminalisation of attempted suicide and introduce support for affected persons. The President said the transmission was made pursuant to Section 58(2) of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, as amended. The letter, titled, “Transmission of the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026 for Consideration,” reads in part: “I forward, herewith, the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026 for the kind consideration of the House of Representatives.” Explaining the objective of the proposed amendment, Tinubu stated that the bill “seeks to amend the National Mental Health Act, No. 46, 2021 (the ‘Principal Act’) to decriminalise attempted suicide and to provide support to any person who attempts to commit suicide in Nigeria.” He expressed appreciation to the House of Representatives and urged lawmakers to give the proposed legislation expeditious consideration. The proposed amendment, if passed by the National Assembly and assented to by the President, would change the existing legal framework governing attempted suicide in Nigeria, shifting the approach towards support for affected persons. The bill is expected to be considered by the House in line with its legislative procedures. item.title: Falana urges FG to pursue £420m British reparations, withdraw appeal
item.description: Human rights lawyer, Femi Falana, SAN, has urged the Federal Government to mount diplomatic pressure on the British Government to pay £420 million in damages awarded by a Federal High Court to the families of 21 coal miners killed in the 1949 Iva Valley massacre in Enugu State. Falana also called on the Federal Government to withdraw its appeal against the judgment, arguing that the British Government had not challenged the historic decision. He made the call in a statement marking the 75th anniversary of the massacre, in which 21 Nigerian coal miners were shot dead by colonial authorities during a protest against harsh working conditions, racial discrimination in wages and unpaid back wages. The judgment was delivered by Justice Anthony Onovo of the Federal High Court in the suit, Mazi Greg Onoh v. Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs & Ors (Suit No. E/909/2024). Justice Onovo held the British colonial administration liable for the killings, describing the massacre as an unlawful and extrajudicial violation of the right to life. The court ordered the British Government to pay £20 million to the families of each of the 21 deceased miners, amounting to £420 million in compensation. The judge found that the miners were defenceless and were merely demanding improved working conditions when they were shot, stressing that they were not engaged in any violent action against the authorities. The court also awarded post-judgment interest of 10 per cent per annum on the compensation until full payment, while claims for pre-judgment interest and exemplary damages were waived. In addition, Justice Onovo ordered the British Government to issue unreserved written apologies to the victims’ families through their counsel. The apologies are to be published in Nigeria’s Daily Sun, Daily Independent and The Punch, as well as three major national newspapers in the United Kingdom. The court directed that evidence of the publications be filed within 60 days, while the monetary awards must be satisfied within 90 days of the judgment. Justice Onovo further held that the Federal Government and the Attorney-General of the Federation had a constitutional responsibility under Sections 19(d) and 150(1) to pursue redress for the victims. He faulted the prolonged failure of the Nigerian authorities to seek justice for the deceased miners, describing the inaction as a dereliction of their constitutional responsibility. The judge consequently directed the Federal Government to initiate and pursue diplomatic engagement with the British authorities within 60 days to secure justice, effective remedies and reparations. Falana urged the Federal Government to concentrate on enforcing the judgment rather than pursuing an appeal, insisting that the families of the slain miners deserved justice and compensation for the killings. item.title: Police seek relatives of man killed in Lagos airport road crash
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Following a fatal road accident on Friday, November 13, 2026, the Airport Police Command, Ikeja, has called for assistance in identifying the family, relatives and friends of a male victim, Abraham Osakpolor, who died in the incident. The accident occurred along the expressway leading from the Murtala Muhammed International Airport towards the Oshodi axis of Lagos. Osakpolor, who was born in Benin City, Edo State, on September 1, 1968, was hit by a moving vehicle and subsequently rushed to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The command’s Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Mohammed Adeola, in a statement, said the deceased’s remains had been deposited in the hospital morgue The statement reads: “The motorist involved in the accident was immediately apprehended by the Airport Police Command and will be charged to court. “During an initial search of the deceased’s belongings, a Nigerian passport with passport number B51930694 and a mobile device without a SIM card were recovered. The mortuary attendants subsequently informed the Command that a Canadian passport with passport number AE763025 had also been discovered among his belongings during a further search. Despite concerted efforts by the Police to establish contact with his family or persons who may know him, these efforts have so far proved unsuccessful. “The command is therefore urgently calling on members of the public, particularly those who may know the deceased or have information about his family, relatives or associates, to assist in notifying them of this unfortunate incident. “The public is also encouraged to share and circulate this information widely to ensure it reaches anyone who may be able to identify the deceased and facilitate contact with his family. Anyone with useful information is urged to contact the Airport Police Command through the following channels: Airport Police Command, X: @airportcommand and Facebook: Airport Command.” The post Police seek relatives of man killed in Lagos airport road crash appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US applauds Nigerian troops for rescuing 125 kidnap victims
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The United States has commended Nigerian troops for rescuing 125 kidnap victims during military operations across the country between November 6 and 12. The US Bureau of African Affairs gave the commendation in a statement posted on its X handle on Wednesday, also praising the troops for dismantling terrorist camps, recovering weapons and clearing explosive devices. “The United States commends Nigerian military operations this month that have rescued 125 kidnapping victims, along with the dismantling of Islamic terrorist camps, the recovery of weapons, and clearance of explosive devices,” the statement read. The bureau said Washington supported the Federal Government’s efforts to prevent kidnappings and ensure those responsible were brought to justice. “We support all efforts by the Nigerian government to prevent kidnappings and hold the perpetrators of this violence fully accountable,” it added. The Defence Headquarters had earlier disclosed that troops rescued the 125 victims during operations conducted between November 6 and 12. It said the troops also killed eight terrorists and arrested 10 suspected collaborators and logistics suppliers during the operations. The military said the largest rescue operation took place in Borno State, where troops freed 119 travellers abducted on November 6 along the Dutsen Kura-Bulazarma-Kamuya Road in Buratai, Biu Local Government Area. According to the military, the attackers abandoned the captives while fleeing from pursuing troops. Those rescued comprised 69 men, 35 women and 15 children. Troops also rescued five kidnapped persons in separate operations in Zamfara State. The military further disclosed that 12 terrorist fighters and members of their families surrendered during the operations. item.title: UK warns visa applicants against four fraud red flags
item.description: The United Kingdom Visas and Immigration (UKVI) agency has warned foreign nationals applying for British visas to watch out for four warning signs that could indicate fraud. The agency issued the advisory in a post on its X handle on Wednesday, urging applicants to protect themselves against visa scams and fraudulent agents. “4 RED FLAGS to watch out for when applying for a UK visa. Protect yourself from visa fraud by learning these crucial warning signs in our infographic,” UKVI said. The warning signs include individuals who guarantee applicants UK visas or jobs, offer appointments or visa services that cannot be verified through official channels, make unsolicited contact to demand money or personal information, and pressure applicants to act immediately or keep transactions secret. According to the agency, scammers operate through phone calls, websites, emails and social media platforms, while some also approach unsuspecting applicants outside visa application centres. It said fraudsters often impersonate Home Office officials or representatives of visa application centres, offering to secure jobs, arrange appointments or process visa applications. Some also claim that there is a problem with an applicant’s visa and demand urgent payment to prevent its cancellation or possible deportation. UKVI warned that fraudsters could use official-sounding language and forged documents, including seemingly genuine job offer letters, to convince applicants to part with their money. The agency also cautioned against agents who promise to fast-track visa applications in exchange for payments into personal bank accounts. “Visa officers will never ask you for money in person, by email or phone,” the guidance stated. It added that applicants seeking UK visas or permission to travel would never be asked to pay visa fees through email, at a visa application centre or into a personal bank account. The agency advised applicants to book appointments through the official UK government website or its authorised commercial partner. It further warned that submitting forged documents could result in visa refusal and a 10-year ban on future UK visa applications. UKVI urged applicants who suspect fraud not to disclose personal information, surrender their passports or send money, gift cards or vouchers to suspected scammers. It advised victims and individuals who suspect fraud in the UK to report the incidents to Report Fraud, while those outside the country should contact their local authorities. Visa fraud remains a concern for international travellers, with applicants sometimes losing money to fraudulent agents and unauthorised service providers. item.title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries for House speaker
item.description: US Democrats on Wednesday elected Hakeem Jeffries as their leader and nominee for Speaker of the House of Representatives, putting him on course to become the first Black politician to occupy the powerful position. The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot, with 11 votes cast against his nomination, according to US media reports. Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressive lawmakers exposed divisions within the Democratic Party over how to exercise its newfound power following a sweeping midterm election victory. His nomination positions him to preside over a commanding Democratic majority during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, as the party prepares to reverse Republican policies and launch investigations into the administration. However, Jeffries must still secure a formal vote of the full House when the new Congress convenes on January 3. With Democrats holding a large majority, his election is widely expected to be a formality. Both returning Democrats and incoming lawmakers participated in Wednesday’s leadership election, including progressives who had sought concessions on issues ranging from US military support for Israel to the influence of money in politics. Jeffries had requested a recorded vote rather than a nomination by acclamation, a process that would have allowed the party to endorse him without a formal ballot. He argued that every Democrat should have the opportunity to assess his experience, record and vision, citing the precedent set when the party last took control of the House in 2018. Although the overall voting figures were made public, individual ballots remained secret. Ahead of the election, Jeffries met with progressive lawmakers to discuss issues including Israel and healthcare. Proposals to lower the Medicare eligibility age and expand healthcare coverage were among the issues considered. The Democratic leader has also sought to shift attention to his party’s governing agenda following the Republican defeat, amid voter dissatisfaction over the Iran war and rising fuel costs. “Folks are drowning in this Republican economy, and House Democrats are committed to turning that situation around, beginning on day one,” he told reporters on Tuesday. “We’re going to relentlessly fight for an affordable America.” Brooklyn roots Raised in the working-class Crown Heights neighbourhood of Brooklyn, New York, Jeffries trained as a lawyer before entering the New York State Legislature in 2007. He was elected to Congress in 2012. Known for his measured manner, sharp rhetoric and frequent references to hip-hop artists, he made history in 2022 when Democrats elected him to succeed Nancy Pelosi as their House leader, making him the first Black politician to lead a party in either chamber of Congress. item.title: Reps demand NNPCL accountability, warn on PIA implementation
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for stronger accountability in the petroleum sector, warning that poor implementation of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) could undermine the reforms intended to transform the industry. The House said the success of the reforms would depend on transparency, institutional discipline and responsible corporate governance. The position was reinforced at a conference on PIA implementation organised by the House in collaboration with the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and other partners in Abuja. Speaking after the conference, Deputy Spokesman of the House, Philip Agbese, commended NNPCL Group Chief Executive Officer, Bayo Ojulari, for promoting transparency and constructive engagement with the National Assembly. Agbese, a Labour Party member representing a constituency in Benue State, said engagement between the legislature and the national oil company was necessary to ensure that the objectives of the PIA translated into measurable improvements in the petroleum industry. He urged other government agencies to adopt similar open-door approaches in their dealings with the legislature, stressing that transparency and institutional collaboration were essential to effective governance. The conference, themed, “Petroleum Industry Act Implementation: The PIA, Corporate Governance and Legislative Oversight,” was organised in collaboration with the Office of the Speaker of the House, Rep. Abbas Tajudeen. Declaring the conference open, Abbas, who was represented by the House Leader, Julius Ihonvbere, said the PIA was designed to establish a transparent, commercially viable, accountable and investment-friendly petroleum industry. He, however, warned that the enactment of the law alone would not guarantee the desired reforms without effective implementation. The Speaker said the transformation of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation into a commercially oriented company, the establishment of independent regulatory institutions and the introduction of a host community development framework were intended to address longstanding structural weaknesses in the industry. He stressed that NNPCL’s commercial autonomy must be matched with corporate accountability, noting that the freedom to make business decisions must come with responsibility for their consequences. Abbas also cautioned against turning legislative oversight into unnecessary interference in the company’s legitimate commercial operations, saying oversight should promote transparency, protect public resources and ensure compliance with statutory responsibilities. He identified crude oil theft, pipeline vandalism, production constraints, infrastructure deficiencies, investment uncertainty and regulatory bottlenecks as major challenges confronting the industry. item.title: Viral Video: ‘We recovered 12 AK-47 rifles, kidnap victims’ – Military defends engagement with bandits
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The military has defended its engagement with armed bandits in Kwara State, dismissing allegations of fraternisation with terrorists. They added that the interaction led to the recovery of 12 AK-47 rifles and the release of 10 kidnapped persons. The Joint Task Force, Operation Savannah Shield, said the engagement, captured in a video circulating on social media, was part of a security initiative to recover illegal weapons and secure the freedom of abducted persons. In a statement, the task force said the interaction involving military personnel, Department of State Services (DSS) operatives and the armed bandits should not be misconstrued as a compromise of the Armed Forces’ responsibilities. The statement, signed by the Acting Deputy Director, Army Public Relations, 9 Division/Operation Savannah Shield, Lieutenant Colonel Ibrahim Shittu, said the armed elements had indicated their willingness to surrender their weapons and release their captives. Shittu said the development followed sustained military operations that had put the bandits under intense pressure, leaving them with the options of surrendering or being neutralised. He said the engagement resulted in the recovery of 12 AK-47 rifles and the release of 10 kidnapped persons. The task force described the outcome as evidence of the effectiveness of its non-kinetic approach, which complements ongoing military offensives against terrorism and banditry. It explained that its operational strategy combined military action, intelligence-driven engagements and other non-kinetic measures to address security challenges. The task force added that individuals willing to surrender would undergo appropriate security screening and other applicable legal procedures. Shittu also said surrendered combatants must not be harmed at the point of surrender, in line with the Law of Armed Conflict, international best practices and established rules of engagement. He stressed that accepting the surrender of armed elements was a recognised and legitimate military outcome, not an indication of unprofessional conduct or compromise. The task force reaffirmed the Armed Forces’ commitment to defending Nigeria’s territorial integrity and protecting lives and property. It urged members of the public to disregard what it described as misleading interpretations of the video and avoid spreading unverified information capable of undermining ongoing security operations. Operation Savannah Shield assured Nigerians that it would continue to provide updates on its activities through its official communication channels. item.title: Army commissions 20 transit flats, officers’ mess in Bauchi
item.description: By Henry Obetta The Nigerian Army has commissioned 20 transit flats and a modern officers’ mess at Obienu Barracks, Bauchi State, as part of efforts to improve personnel welfare, boost troops’ morale and enhance operational effectiveness. The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, who commissioned the facilities on Wednesday, said the Army’s modernisation drive went beyond the acquisition of military equipment to include improved accommodation, infrastructure and welfare for personnel and their families. According to a statement by the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, Shaibu described decent accommodation and a conducive living environment as critical to troops’ morale, family stability and operational readiness. He explained that the 20 transit flats were designed to address accommodation challenges faced by personnel posted to the barracks for assignments, military courses and other temporary engagements. The COAS said the newly constructed officers’ mess, named the Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu Officers’ Mess, featured modern accommodation, a Hall of Fame and recreational facilities to promote professional interaction, esprit de corps and institutional pride among officers. He commended the Nigerian Army Armoured Corps and other stakeholders for the successful completion of the projects, describing them as evidence of the Army’s commitment to personnel welfare and prudent management of resources. Shaibu urged personnel to ensure proper maintenance of the facilities to guarantee their sustainability and continued usefulness. Reaffirming his commitment to the welfare of troops and their families, the Army chief said investments in accommodation, healthcare, education and other welfare programmes would continue alongside the force’s expansion and modernisation efforts. He stressed that a well-motivated, professionally trained and adequately supported force was essential to sustaining operational successes against terrorism, insurgency, banditry and other security threats facing the country. item.title: Tinubu’s economic gains bypass ordinary Nigerians, Makinde campaign tells Alake
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation has faulted the Minister of Solid Minerals, Dele Alake, over his defence of President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies, saying the reforms have delivered gains for government institutions and corporate interests but little relief to ordinary Nigerians. The organisation said increased federation revenue, foreign exchange reforms and the clearance of outstanding foreign exchange obligations had not translated into better living conditions, as millions of Nigerians continued to struggle with rising food prices, transportation costs, electricity tariffs and school fees. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the organisation was responding to Alake’s challenge to Nigerians to name any civilian administration that had achieved more across the socio-economic and political spectrum within three years or identify a viable alternative to Tinubu’s economic reforms introduced in May 2023. Ihediwa accused the minister of measuring economic progress through macroeconomic and institutional adjustments while overlooking the daily struggles of ordinary Nigerians. “For the average Nigerian, prosperity was not shared; austerity was distributed universally,” he said. While acknowledging that previous administrations lacked the political will to remove petrol subsidy and unify the exchange rate, the campaign organisation faulted Tinubu for implementing the reforms simultaneously without adequate social protection measures. It argued that combining subsidy removal with currency devaluation and electricity tariff increases imposed multiple economic shocks on households without sufficient measures to cushion their effects. “Taking the bullet is admirable only if you protect the citizens standing behind you,” Ihediwa said. On petrol subsidy removal, the organisation agreed that the previous arrangement was unsustainable and vulnerable to corruption but argued that the government should have provided mass transit alternatives, strengthened domestic refining capacity and introduced effective measures to contain transportation costs before or alongside the policy. It also questioned Alake’s description of the clearance of $7 billion in foreign exchange backlogs and restoration of international card transactions as benefits of exchange rate unification. According to Ihediwa, those gains primarily addressed the concerns of foreign investors, multinational companies and corporate institutions, rather than the immediate needs of Nigerians struggling with the cost of living. He argued that celebrating improved corporate foreign exchange liquidity while local manufacturers battled high borrowing costs and exchange rate volatility reflected a disconnect between the government’s economic priorities and the realities of citizens. item.title: Explosion heard in Riyadh, Saudi capital; missiles intercepted
item.description: A powerful explosion rattled homes in Riyadh on Wednesday, AFP journalists and residents said, as Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis pressed their campaign of attacks against the kingdom. The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis also said they intercepted two cruise missiles — the latest in weeks of strikes targeting military, civilian and oil infrastructure. Later on Wednesday, the coalition said it had intercepted two drones launched by the Houthis in the Riyadh and southern regions, after Saudi authorities had issued and later lifted an alert for the southern Sharurah governorate. Residents said Wednesday’s explosion came without warning, with no mobile-phone alert issued beforehand as is usually the case during aerial threats. “The explosion was extremely loud,” said a resident in northern Riyadh. “Hearing a blast without receiving a warning is very frightening.” An AFP journalist said doors throughout her home swung open and the lights briefly went out. The location of the explosion was not immediately clear, but residents told AFP they saw smoke near Riyadh’s airport in the northeast of the city. In October, a deadly attack targeting Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport killed 14 people and injured hundreds, forcing the suspension of flights for two weeks. Within minutes, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said its air defences had intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by the group towards the Riyadh region. Earlier, the coalition had reported intercepting another cruise missile also heading for the same region. Saudi civil defence authorities also said they had activated early warning systems in the southern regions of Jazan, Najran and Khamis Mushait, near the Yemeni border. The Saudi-led coalition, which backs neighbouring Yemen’s internationally recognised government in its war with the Houthis, has battled a surge in attacks since hostilities reignited in July. The long-running civil war in Yemen, one of the world’s poorest countries, had been largely dormant after a ceasefire went into effect in 2022. The Houthis are now nearing Aden, the government’s interim capital, having made sweeping territorial gains since the war resumed. Since the summer, more than 1,600 people have been killed and over 300,000 displaced by the fighting, according to the United Nations. item.title: ADC, Kaduna gov’t differ over venue
item.description: From Mohammed Ibrahim Yaba, Kaduna; Hussein Yahaya, Baba Martins & Daniel Adaji, Abuja The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the Kaduna State Government of denying the party the use of the Ranchers Bees Stadium to host the Northwest rally of its presidential campaign. The party said it had applied to use the stadium for its rally scheduled for November 17 and 18 but was refused access to the facility by the state government, which denied the claim. The ADC National Vice Chairman, North-West, Hafsat Baba, told one of our correspondents that the party dutifully informed the state government of its intention to use the facility, but the latter turned down its request. Daily Trust reports that the All Progressives Congress (APC) recently held its presidential campaign flag-off at the same venue. In a letter dated November 12, 2026 reportedly from the Kaduna State Ministry of Local Government Affairs and addressed to the Office of the National Vice Chairman of the ADC, North-West, the ministry said the stadium would not be available on the requested dates due to ongoing repairs. The letter, signed by Mohammed Sani Haruna, Senior Special Assistant to the Commissioner, stated: “We write to acknowledge receipt of your letter with the above caption. However, we regret to inform you that due to ongoing repairs at the stadium, it will not be available for the aforementioned programme on the dates requested by you.” Baba said the ADC also notified security agencies, including the Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Inspector-General of Police, Kaduna State Police Command and the General Officer Commanding, about the planned rally. “We sent these letters not only to state security agencies but also to their national offices, just to be on the safe side,” she said. Baba explained that the party initially considered the Ahmadu Bello Stadium but was informed that it was under construction and subsequently considered the Trade Fair Complex but was also told that the facility would not be available. She said the party decided to request Ranchers Bees Stadium after learning that the APC had recently used it for its presidential campaign flag-off. “We were aware that Ahmadu Bello Stadium was under construction. We then thought of using the Trade Fair Complex, but we were made to understand that it would also not be available. We knew that they (APC) used Ranchers Bees recently, so we decided to request it, but it was denied,” she said. The ADC chieftain questioned why its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, should be prevented from holding a rally in Kaduna, which she described as his second home. “If Atiku can visit Bauchi and Yobe and hold his rallies, why can’t he come to Kaduna, his second home, because he has a house here?” she asked. item.title: Gaming Phenomenon ‘Grand Theft Auto’ Goes Live After 13-Year Wait
item.description: After 13 years of waiting, including two delays and several leaks, the first gamers began playing Wednesday the latest instalment of “Grand Theft Auto”, the most expensive — and among the most profitable — video game ever developed. “GTA VI” becomes available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles at midnight Thursday in each region where it will be available. That meant it launched first in New Zealand (at 1100 GMT on Wednesday), with many players around the world changing their console location settings to the far-eastern country to be among the first to enter the new Vice City. “I’ve been playing GTA for such a long time that the anticipation for this is crazy,” Australian student Riley Fennel told AFP ahead of the launch. Although Rockstar Games, the studio behind GTA, has not yet released advance unit sales figures, specialist firm Sensor Tower estimates they have already surpassed 15 million. That would be more than $1.5 billion in revenue before the game even came out, for a budget estimated at $1 billion to $1.5 billion, which would be unprecedented. According to the British analytics firm Omdia, sales of “GTA VI” could reach $3.2 billion by the end of the year. An organiser fixes a poster of the video game ‘Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI’ ahead of its launch party in Chennai on November 17, 2026. Photo by R.SATISH BABU / AFP ‘Taylor Swift of games’ “No other concert or box office release has ever generated that much capital. And so that makes it one of the outliers in entertainment,” said Joost van Dreunen, a professor at New York University’s Stern School of Business. “This is the Taylor Swift of video games,” the industry specialist said. Rockstar’s parent company, US publisher Take-Two Interactive, has rolled out a massive marketing campaign to establish the title as a mass cultural product that transcends the boundaries of video games. “The reach of the game is such that it will lead to a downstream effect on engagement on other entertainment services,” such as streaming platforms, said James McWhirter at Omdia. “I’m going to take four days off,” said Dmytro Shkambara, a 27-year-old Ukrainian player living in Berlin, who said he had been planning this first game session “for a very long time”. Like him, many fans have already booked time off to immerse themselves in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida. The human resources platform Remote said it had seen a 32 percent increase in leave requests around the world for November 19. Touted as bigger, better and more realistic than its predecessors, “GTA VI” follows the adventures of a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style couple trying to survive in the Miami-inspired, crime-ravaged Vice City. Since its beginnings, the series has won players over with its increasingly realistic reconstructions of fictionalised cities and the great freedom of action offered in a highly detailed open world.
